scope: Finite independent GNU differential qualification of the native default and explicitly enabled experimental fd routes, including expressions, metadata, formatting, descriptors and bounded physical preorder prune/quit. No universal speed or filesystem-race equivalence claim.

executionPolicy.publicDefault: Execute original GNU before Node startup, argument proofs or preparatory probes.
executionPolicy.privateDefault: Execute command find with original arguments before Node or preparatory probes.
executionPolicy.PiDefault: Keep the native Bash tool without a wrapper hook; experimental adaptation additionally requires an allowed provider.
executionPolicy.actionPolicy: User command, mutating and output-file actions retain original GNU execution; actions are never timed twice.

experimentalSemanticScope.inProcess: fd candidates with byte-safe filters and Boolean/output evaluation, restored to GNU operand and traversal order.
experimentalSemanticScope.batchedGNU: fd discovery followed by scan-free roots or nonrecursive GNU metadata, matching and formatting evaluation; compile, evaluation, discovery and original fallback invocations are counted separately.
experimentalSemanticScope.incrementalGNU: Physical preorder pure predicates/output plus prune/quit, with finite leading maxdepth and a proved path budget. GNU evaluates the current node before immediate-child fd discovery. Root-only controls require no fd query.
experimentalSemanticScope.incrementalFaultPolicy: Preparation failure uses original GNU before output. After broker start, failed fd directory queries continue with local GNU depth-one discovery without replaying prior expressions.
experimentalSemanticScope.remainingBoundaries: Unbounded prune/quit, unsupported traversal/control combinations, unknown filesystem types or nested mounts, unsafe private scratch placement and user actions retain original GNU; no fd contribution is credited.

qualifiedArchive.verification: The same actual npm pack archive was extracted and replayed on desktop and VM with tools/verify.mjs --deep --sdk. The release coordinator confirmed the transferred archive SHA256.

interpretation: GNU is the default because no current fd command class is proved universally faster. Only exact FIND2FD_EXPERIMENTAL_FD=1 enables the deliberately experimental semantic routes; actual fd contribution is not a speed guarantee.
Each environment passed 100 Node groups: 91 core, 2 generated campaigns and 7 SDK scope checks, with no failures, cancellations, skips, todos, timeouts, truncated logs or source changes.

The 3072 distinct seeded CLI cases comprise 2366 batched fd-search plans, 340 scan-free plans, 16 incremental plans and 350 original-native plans. They made 3743 actual fd invocations per environment, with zero mismatches or qualified runtime fallbacks.
The expression campaign has 1536 distinct locale/argv cases and 960 distinct argv vectors, with 2152 contributing fd searches, zero original-native calls and zero mismatches per environment.

The five default-policy groups contain 61 original-native GNU comparisons with no fd or preparatory engine work, plus one explicit experimental comparison requiring real fd. The CLI default starts no Node dispatcher; three direct-API comparisons necessarily execute inside Node. Raw argv, caller descriptors, closed standard descriptors, stdin and owned actions are included.

Focused controls, metadata, formats, aliases, descriptors and fault comparisons are separate diagnostic groups. Replaying a corpus on two environments or in nested extracted/installed package checks does not increase unique-case coverage.

A root-only prune or quit, scan-free root, compile validation or original-native fallback receives no fd traversal credit. Failed injected fd attempts followed by local GNU discovery receive no real-fd credit.

Incremental fault checks observed 14 local GNU discoveries across two exact complete-output comparisons without original-command replay. A 20-level tree with 4440-byte GNU records proves the original-native long-path boundary. Paused output retained an exact 288036-byte GNU result.

Six direct dispatcher signal checks reached 130/143/129 and removed owned private directories. Private Bash process-group checks compare shell-visible status, valid GNU output prefixes and cleanup; raw wait status differs for handled SIGINT exit130 versus native SIGINT termination. PID-only outer-Bash SIGINT remains a separate native behavior boundary.
Output, stderr, exit status and owned side effects are compared with GNU on synthetic trees. This is finite semantic qualification, not proof through arbitrary concurrent filesystem or mount changes.
The packed-artifact diagnostics contain separately rebuilt tar hashes from each environment; the qualifiedArchive SHA256 identifies the transported immutable outer archive.
This record was written after capture and identifies the immutable tested archive and current implementation/test hashes, not a self-referential tarball containing its own hash.

routingPolicy.experimentalScope: Finite semantic routes only; a real fd invocation is not a speed claim.
